newsitem.title: USA: US WCoast diesels rise amid talk of shut ARCO unit.
newsitem.headline: US WCoast diesels rise amid talk of shut ARCO unit.

text.p: Wholesale prices for U.S. West Coast diesels led gains Tuesday, dealers said, amid trader concerns of a hydrotreater problem at Arco's Carson, California, refinery.
But a union official familiar with plant operations said he did not hear about a problem.
ARCO officials could not be reached for comment.
Traders said a rise in ARCO's rack prices this week indicated the unit might be shut.
"They're usually the low rack (price) in Los Angeles and now they're the high rack," a trader said.
State environmental officials also said the refinery did not report any problems.
On Tuesday, low sulphur diesel in Los Angeles rose 1.50 cents a gallon to 72.50/73.50 cents, while CARB grade material jumped about three cents to 82.50/84 cents on the ARCO rumors.
Jet fuel rose about 0.50 cents a gallon to 80/80.75 cents.
CARB gasoline in L.A. was traded at 79.75 cents a gallon and 80.50 cents a gallon, traders said.
